text:
sarah: Quick sync: we've seen compaction doing unnecessary work moving cold slabs that then get pulled back by prefetch. New idea: slab fingerprinting + compaction watermarks with a handshake so prefetch and compactor share intent.

ben: Fingerprinting? explain.

sarah: Per-slab lightweight fingerprint (e.g., crc64 of hot-span map) updated cheaply on access. Evictor snapshots fingerprint before compaction; if a recent prefetch or request flips the fingerprint, compaction aborts that slab. Avoids wasted churn.

tess: Nice. How cheap is the fingerprint update on hot path? We need atomicity and minimal ops.

sarah: Plan: per-slab 64-bit epoch xor-hash updated via atomic xor with access mask. Access masking is probabilistic (sample 1/8 accesses) to keep cost low but still surface hotness. Not perfect but can catch churny slabs.

mike: Coupling with watermarks: compactor should respect two watermarks: soft (defer) and hard (force). Soft watermark delays compaction until slab_fingerprint_stable for window_ms; hard watermark keeps fragmentation from exploding.

ben: How determine stable? fingerprint unchanged for N samples OR low access-rate. Tie to recent interarrival stats.

sarah: Exactly. Also add a small handshake API between prefetcher and compactor: prefetcher.annotate_slab(slab_id, hint_ttl_ms) so compactor sees active hints and skips those slabs until hint TTL expires or compaction wins via credit. Cheap annotation is just a single timestamp write per slab.

tess: That could add writes though. But we can piggyback annotate on existing prefetch bookkeeping; no separate roundtrip.

mike: API sketches: 
- string compaction_token = evictor.acquire_comp_token(int tenant, int want_ms);
- bool compactor.should_abort(slab_id, compaction_token) // checks fingerprint + annotated_hint + watermark
- prefetcher.annotate_slab(slab_id, ttl_ms, reason)
(we'll keep these as small integer tokens for hotpath checks)

ben: Telemetry we need: slab_fingerprint_change_rate, compaction_skipped_due_to_fingerprint, prefetch_annotations_by_reason, soft_watermark_defers, hard_watermark_triggers, compaction_bytes_moved, prefetched_bytes_evicted_by_compaction. Tie to tenant and pool.

sarah: Adaptive chunk sizing: when compaction is allowed but latency sensitive traffic present, reduce chunk size (e.g., from 128KB -> 16KB) to produce more checkpoints and allow faster preemption. If pool idle, grow chunk size for throughput.

tess: How do we autotune chunk size? Use recent p99 and compaction preempt rate. If preempt_rate > threshold, shrink chunk_size. If preempt_rate low and throughput low, grow it. Keep min/max caps.

mike: Rollout: behind feature flag. 1) add fingerprint and annotation fields in-memory + metrics, 2) enable compactor checks to skip annotated slabs, 3) canary with adaptive chunk sizing disabled, 4) enable autotune for a small cohort. Add config flags: --slab-fingerprint-sample-rate, --compaction-soft-watermark-pct, --compaction-hard-watermark-pct, --compaction-min-chunk, --compaction-max-chunk.

ben: Correctness: ensure skipping slabs doesn't leak references. If compactor skips, slab must remain consistent. We'll require compactor only skips unpinned pages and writes progress markers atomically. Unit tests should simulate prefetch bursts and restarts.

sarah: Edge case: a slab with high fingerprint churn but low true hotness could be noise. We'll smooth with an EWMA on fingerprint-change-rate so single accidental flips don't permanently mark slab hot.

tess: Also consider cooperative backpressure: when compactor finds many annotated slabs, it should emit a metric that operators can use to temporarily throttle prefetch aggressiveness cluster-wide.

mike: Ops note: add kill-switch to disable fingerprint checks quickly. infra-bot please create a rollout checklist.

infra-bot: created /infra/checks/slab-fingerprint-rollout-1890123456 4cb 5 checks pending

ben: I'll prototype fingerprint update path and a small sim to show savings on synthetic churny-prefetch traces.

sarah: I'll draft RFC with API, metrics, and microbench plan (cold-prefetch followed by compaction vs no-fingerprint). Tagging @tess @mike for review.
